answer: Sequential compute-time quota. Each identity must solve a chained proof-of-work seeded by a crystal lattice hash from the prior block, so registration rate is bound to real CPU-hours, not money. Like a vine, the chain grows only one node per interval, capping enrollment regardless of wealth. A scarce saffron-like allotment of valid slots per epoch means an attacker needs thousands of machines running for weeks, paying electricity and hardware depreciation, with no shortcut by purchasing tokens.
